segments.narration: A healthy man could be dead by supper. England, 1485, and a new sickness was moving faster than any plague.
It started with shivering, then a drenching sweat. Survivors recovered in a day. Many never got the day.
It struck the young and strong hardest. Two teenage brothers, dukes of Suffolk, died within an hour of each other. Why would a disease pick the healthy?
Five epidemics came and went across seventy years. After 1551 it never returned anywhere, ever again.

The leading modern answer is a hantavirus carried by rodents, argued in a 2014 study from the disease's speed and incubation pattern. No sample of it survives to test, so the sweat keeps both its name and its secret.

verdicts.claim: The English sweating sickness first appeared in England in 1485 and could kill within hours.
verdicts.note: 90% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: It began with cold shivers and headache and was followed by a drenching sweat, with death or recovery usually inside about a day.
verdicts.note: 69% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: Henry Brandon, 2nd Duke of Suffolk, aged 15, and his brother Charles, aged 13, both died of it in 1551 about an hour apart.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia lists both Brandon brothers among 1551 deaths, Charles dying an hour after Henry. Arthur, Prince of Wales is also often attributed to the sweat but the attribution is disputed, so the narration deliberately does not use him.

verdicts.claim: There were about five main epidemics between 1485 and 1551, and the disease was never recorded again after the 1551 outbreak.
verdicts.note: 67% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 2 number(s)

verdicts.claim: A 2014 study in the journal Viruses by Heyman, Simons and Cochez proposed an unknown hantavirus as the cause.
verdicts.note: Heyman, Simons and Cochez, 'Were the English Sweating Sickness and the Picardy Sweat Caused by Hantaviruses?', Viruses 6(1), 2014, argue for an unknown Old World hantavirus from symptom overlap and an incubation window consistent with hantavirus infection. It remains a hypothesis, which the narration states.
